# Model card: `afib_logreg_v1`

*Generated by `make report` from `docs/templates/MODEL_CARD.template.md`. Every number comes from `results/`
or `configs/default.yaml` (sources: `results/readme_numbers.json`).*

> **Research prototype and decision-support tool. Not a medical device and not a diagnosis.** Not validated
> in astronauts, in microgravity or on a real Holter. Trained and tested only on public, terrestrial,
> resting clinical ECGs. These are not NASA or astronaut data.

## Model details

- **Task:** classify one 9.6-s window of single-lead ECG (lead I, 250 Hz, 2,400 samples) as atrial
  fibrillation (AFIB) vs. sinus rhythm. Sinus bradycardia and sinus tachycardia are negatives.
- **Type:** L2-regularised logistic regression on 30 hand-crafted features (RR irregularity, P-wave /
  atrial activity, QRS morphology, spectrum), median imputation with missing-value indicators,
  standardisation, Platt calibration. Chosen by a pre-registered rule over random forest, LightGBM and a
  compact 1D CNN (simplest model within 0.010 validation AUPRC of the best).
- **System around it:** a signal-quality gate (`SINAL_RUIM`), an out-of-distribution / low-confidence state
  (`INCERTO`), 3-of-3 temporal voting for `ALERTA_AFIB`, and a heart-rate rule for mild
  warnings (defaults 60 / 100 bpm, adapted to personal history).
- **Artifacts:** `models/afib_logreg_v1.json` (34 KB; numpy-only inference via `src/inference.py`)
  and `models/afib_logreg_v1.onnx` (0.8 KB). Metadata include the training commit, the selection
  record and SHA-256 hashes of the source datasets.
- **Input invariance:** offset and scale are removed per window (tested). Raw positive 12-bit A/D
  values from the target device are accepted directly.

## Intended use

On-board, real-time **early detection of the rhythm present in the current window** during continuous
single-lead ECG recording, to support (not replace) a clinician or flight surgeon. Intended context for
this prototype: research and demonstration (NASA Space Apps Challenge).

**Out of scope:** diagnosis; prediction of future AFIB; myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest or
ventricular arrhythmias (no coverage); atrial flutter (often misclassified, see below); paediatric use;
any clinical deployment.

## Training and evaluation data

- **Training:** Chapman-Shaoxing part of PhysioNet *ecg-arrhythmia* v1.0.0 (Shaoxing only, because the
  Ningbo part has no AFIB), training split of a record-level split (no patient IDs available).
- **Internal test:** held-out Shaoxing split (1,230 windows, 261 AFIB).
- **External test:** all of PTB-XL v1.0.3 with AFIB or sinus labels (1,428 AFIB, 15,877 non-AFIB).
- **Stress tests:** Ningbo sinus records, out-of-training rhythms, real noise (MIT-BIH NSTDB).

## Metrics (per window, thresholds frozen on Shaoxing validation)

| Test set | AUROC | Sensitivity [95% CI] | Specificity [95% CI] | PPV | PPV at 1% prevalence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Internal (Shaoxing) | 0.9998 | 1.000 [1.000–1.000] | 0.988 [0.980–0.994] | 0.956 | 0.449 |
| External (PTB-XL) | 0.9968 | 0.990 [0.985–0.995] | 0.957 [0.954–0.960] | 0.677 | – |
| RR baseline, internal | 0.9947 | 0.992 | 0.985 | 0.945 | 0.393 |

Calibration: ECE 0.0030 internal and 0.013 external, but externally the intermediate
probabilities are overconfident (0.5–0.9 predicted → 3%–24% observed AFIB). Simulated false alerts per day with 3-of-3
voting on PTB-XL: 0.01 if windows were independent, 4.0 with correlated errors, and
53–179 for a person with frequent ectopy.

## Known failure modes

- **Specificity drops out of distribution** (0.988 → 0.957 on PTB-XL). At the frozen
  operating point the RR baseline makes fewer errors than this model on PTB-XL.
- **Look-alike rhythms are called AFIB:** atrial flutter 55%, atrial tachycardia 44%, ectopy up to
  31%, sinus arrhythmia up to 21% of windows.
- **Altered rate outside the training source:** false-AFIB rate 9.2% in PTB-XL sinus bradycardia
  and 6.6% in sinus tachycardia.
- **Noise:** under muscle noise at −6 dB, specificity is 0.367 without SQI and 0.547 with the
  recalibrated SQI.

## Bias and subgroups

AFIB patients in the data are much older than sinus patients (age is a strong confounder). In the internal test,
the astronaut-like age band (30–54 years) has only 19 AFIB windows (sensitivity
1.000, specificity 0.994 [0.986–1.000]). Specificity is lower in patients aged 70+
(0.978). Populations: Chinese (Shaoxing) training data and German (PTB-XL) external data. Other
ancestries, healthy young adults, exercise, posture changes and microgravity are not represented.

## Ethical considerations

A false sense of security (missed AFIB) and alarm fatigue (false alerts) are both possible. The model must not
drive treatment decisions. Outputs should go to a qualified clinician together with the raw ECG.
